knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,

library(suppose)

After reviewing a regression, the next useful question may be where a new
measurement would change your understanding most. Suppose compares explicit,
feasible alternatives under that retained model. It does not conduct experiments.

This workflow requires an optional alloptr build exporting
`bed_normal_contrast()`. The score is an exact calculation for the supported
normal/inverse-gamma model; it does not train a learned design policy.

## Decide what you want to learn

There are two supported purposes:

| Purpose | Target | Cost units |
|---|---|---|
| Estimate | Reduce expected squared error for a mean contrast | Squared outcome units |
| Decide | Reduce expected opportunity loss between two protocols | Outcome-equivalent utility units |

For a decision, the preference threshold is the outcome-equivalent penalty for
choosing the second protocol. A practically useful strength gain is not, by
itself, a conversion from time or money into utility. State that tradeoff explicitly.

## Describe alternatives in original units

Continue from the retained `record` at the end of the
[regression tutorial](regression.html). These example calls are not run on this
page because they depend on that record and the optional alloptr method.

```{r candidates, eval=FALSE}
contrast <- data.frame(temperature = c(140, 160), duration = c(60, 60))
candidates <- data.frame(
  candidate_id = c("low-1", "high-1", "low-6", "high-6"),
  temperature = c(140, 160, 140, 160),
  duration = 60,
  repeats = c(1, 1, 6, 6),
  cost = 0,
  feasible = TRUE
)
plan <- design_regression(
  record,
  regression_id = tail(record$regressions, 1)[[1]]$id,
  candidates = candidates,
  contrast = contrast,
  purpose = "estimate",
  max_units = 6,
  rationale = "Compare independent preparations; omit costs explicitly under a six-unit budget."
)
```

The target is the second contrast row minus the first. Each candidate is a
separate alternative experiment, with independent replicates at one setting.
It is not a batch containing all candidate rows. Zero costs compare learning
benefits under the unit budget alone.

## Review before retaining

Inspect eligibility, expected benefit, net benefit, ties, extrapolation flags,
and inherited model-check limitations. A precise design score can still rest on
an inadequate scientific model.

`record_research_design()` retains a chosen candidate ID, reviewer, and reason.
You can retain `"none"` if none is appropriate. In the workbench,
**Plan the next measurement** provides the preview and review controls.

A saved plan is neither an executed experiment nor a frozen prospective test.
Use the [continue, test and sensitivity guide](research-loop.html) to resume a
reviewed plan, freeze a regression prediction, attach future measurements, or
review assumption dependence. Multi-setting batch optimization, interactions,
and general nonlinear models remain outside the planning method.
